newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares mixed on options speculation.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares mixed on options speculation.

text.p: Israeli shares closed mixed on Wednesday with a negative bias as options speculators rocked the market, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 0.38 percent, or 0.74 points, to 196.57 on an all-share turnover of 82 million shekels against 100 million on Tuesday.
The Maof 25 index lost 0.29 percent to 206.32.

"Trading was very mixed and the most active players were the Maof options speculators who were trying to influence trading before the expiration of options on Thursday," said Geualien Assous at Sahar Securities.
"If it was not for the options players the market would have probably closed a little lower because of profit taking," Assous said.
Osem Investments rose 2.25 percent to 1,902. The company said it finalised an agreement together with Tnuva Co-Op to form a joint venture for the production of ice cream.

Venture capital fund Mofet surged 6.0 percent to 148 following news that Orchit Communication's initial public offering on Nasdaq is expected to be priced on Wednesday or Thursday at $14 to $16 a share. Mofet holds a 4.3 percent stake in Orchit.
Africa Israel Investments fell 1.50 percent to 390,683. Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull Securities rated the company a buy despite a recent rally.

"The market was very sleepy today with no special activity. Stocks traded in a narrow range and most investors are waiting to see which direction the market will take," said a trader at Bank Hapoalim.
"The minimal reduction in interest rates shows that the central bank will keep interest rates at the current level. Investors are disappointed and many of them remained sidelined," he said.
On Tuesday the Bank of Israel lowered its key lending rate for October by 0.3 percentage point to an annualised nominal rate of 15.5 percent.

The most active shares were Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which gained 0.5 percent to 144,593 on volume of 11 million shekels; Koor Industries, which rose 1.75 percent to 29,431 on turnover of 6.0 million shekels; and Super Sol, which rose 2.50 percent to 7,468 on volume of five million shekels.
